purpose: One anchor reading selection per geometry unit, integrated through a three-stage reading arc: Read & Notice, Math Connection, Evidence & Synthesis.
calendar_note: The live course is 36 weeks with mixed unit lengths. The reading arc is a three-stage instructional sequence, not a requirement that every math unit occupy exactly three weeks.
mastery_policy: Reading activities enrich geometry, vocabulary, evidence use, and critical thinking but do not replace the 80% mathematics mastery gate.
source_policy: Prefer public-domain, openly licensed, or legitimately free-access sources. Preserve attribution and provide accessible excerpts/reading guides.

integration_pattern.stage_1: Read & Notice: context, author, vocabulary, mathematical ideas, questions.
integration_pattern.stage_2: Math Connection: connect one claim, diagram, method, historical problem, or idea directly to unit mathematics.
integration_pattern.stage_3: Evidence & Synthesis: short evidence-citation response, critical-thinking prompt, design reflection, or model critique.

units.title: Foundations, Constructions & Geometric Reasoning
units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid
units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
units.selection: Introduction; Book I definitions, postulates/common notions, and selected opening propositions
units.connection: Definitions, axioms/postulates, compass-straightedge construction, proof, and the difference between appearance and deduction.
units.critical_question: What must be accepted, defined, constructed, or proved before a geometric conclusion is trustworthy?

units.title: Transformations, Symmetry & Congruence
units.anchor: Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions
units.author: Edwin A. Abbott
units.selection: Sections 1-3 and selected passages on recognizing figures, motion, dimension, and point of view
units.connection: Shape identity, transformations, perception, invariance, symmetry, and spatial reasoning.
units.critical_question: Which properties belong to a figure itself, and which depend on the observer or representation?

units.title: Triangle Congruence & Proof
units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid
units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
units.selection: Book I, selected triangle-congruence propositions including propositions 4, 8, and 26
units.connection: SSS/SAS/ASA-style reasoning, corresponding parts, and proof from limited measurements.
units.critical_question: How much information is sufficient to force two triangles to agree?

units.title: Parallel Lines, Slopes & Coordinate Proof
units.author: David Hilbert
units.selection: Teacher-curated excerpts on incidence, order, parallels, and the role of axioms
units.connection: Parallelism, logical conditions, proof structure, and why coordinate evidence must satisfy defined relationships.
units.critical_question: Which facts about lines follow from definitions and axioms, and which require additional evidence?

units.title: Similarity, Dilations & Proportional Reasoning
units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid
units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
units.selection: Book VI selections on similar figures and proportional sides
units.connection: Similarity, scale factors, proportional reasoning, indirect measurement, maps, and models.
units.critical_question: What must remain proportional for a scale model to represent the original faithfully?

units.title: Right Triangles, Trigonometry & Bearings
units.author: Harold Jacoby
units.selection: Navigation at Sea and selected passages on astronomical direction-finding
units.connection: Bearings, inaccessible distances, right-triangle measurement, navigation, instruments, and error.
units.critical_question: How can angle and direction measurements determine a position or distance that cannot be measured directly?

units.title: Polygons & Quadrilaterals
units.anchor: Flatland: A Romance of Many Dimensions
units.author: Edwin A. Abbott
units.selection: Selected passages describing triangles, squares, polygons, recognition, and social classification
units.connection: Polygon classification, attributes, necessary/sufficient properties, and the danger of confusing labels with mathematical evidence.
units.critical_question: When does a classification follow from geometric properties, and when is it merely an imposed label?

units.title: Circles, Arcs & Tangency
units.anchor: The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid
units.author: Euclid; John Casey edition
units.selection: Book III selections on circles, chords, tangents, arcs, and angle relationships
units.connection: Circle theorems, tangent relationships, chords, arcs, central/inscribed relationships, and deductive structure.
units.critical_question: Which circle relationships are consequences of radius and symmetry rather than visual appearance?

units.title: Analytic Geometry, Loci & Conic Connections
units.author: W. H. Besant
units.selection: Introductory definitions and selected geometric treatments of ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola
units.connection: Locus definitions, conic sections, distance conditions, construction, and coordinate/geometric representations.
units.critical_question: How can one geometric condition generate an entire curve?

units.title: Area, Measurement & Geometric Probability
units.author: John Venn
units.selection: Chapter I and selected Chapter II passages on probability series, error/divergence, and a line drawn at random
units.connection: Probability, randomness, repeated trials, measurement, uncertainty, and geometric probability.
units.critical_question: When does a measured or observed frequency justify a probability claim, and what uncertainty remains?

units.title: Solids, Surface Area & Volume
units.anchor: Solid Geometry with Problems and Applications
units.author: H. E. Slaught and N. J. Lennes
units.selection: Teacher-curated selections on polyhedra, prisms/cylinders, pyramids/cones, surface area, volume, and cross-sections
units.connection: Nets, dimensional reasoning, surface area versus volume, cross-sections, and design efficiency.
units.critical_question: Why do length, area, and volume scale differently when a solid is enlarged?

units.title: CAD, Scale Drawing & Spatial Design
units.author: John Ruskin
units.selection: Opening instructional sections and selected perspective constructions
units.connection: Technical drawing, representation, viewpoint, spatial design, scale, projection, and the difference between the object and its drawing.
units.critical_question: How does a representation preserve some geometric information while changing other information?

units.title: Geometry Modeling Capstone & Defense
units.author: Henri Poincare
units.selection: Introduction; selected passages from On the Nature of Mathematical Reasoning, Space and Geometry, and Experience and Geometry
units.connection: Constraint, validation, assumptions, models, evidence, uncertainty, sufficiency, and the limits of mathematical claims.
units.critical_question: What does a mathematical model establish, what does it assume, and what evidence would make us revise it?

optional_enrichment.title: The Mathematicall Praeface to Elements of Geometrie
optional_enrichment.author: John Dee

optional_enrichment.title: The Teaching of Geometry
optional_enrichment.author: David Eugene Smith
optional_enrichment.use: Teacher resource and selected student history passages on why geometry is studied, Euclid, definitions, axioms, and applications.

optional_enrichment.title: The Theory and Practice of Perspective
optional_enrichment.author: G. A. Storey
optional_enrichment.use: Alternative/additional Unit 12 reading at approximately 8th-9th grade readability.

optional_enrichment.title: Mathematical Recreations and Essays
optional_enrichment.author: W. W. Rouse Ball
optional_enrichment.use: Optional challenge readings, famous geometry problems, and critical-thinking extensions.
